nodes.name: Execute Workflow Trigger
nodes.notes: Chained from Agent 4 when intent = interested. Can also be exposed as its own webhook.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify((() => { const m = $('GET Agent Prompt (scheduler)').first().json.agent.model; const model = (!m || /nemotron|openrouter/i.test(m)) ? 'gemini-3.5-flash-lite' : m; const isGemma = /^gemma/i.test(model); const body = { model, max_tokens: isGemma ? Math.max(256, 4096) : 256, messages: [{role:'system', content: $('GET Agent Prompt (scheduler)').first().json.agent.systemPrompt}, {role:'user', content: JSON.stringify($('GET Lead').first().json.lead)}] }; return body; })()) }}

nodes.name: Postmark: Send Booking Email
nodes.notes: IMPORTANT: was completely unauthenticated (no credential, no token header, no content-type header at all) -- the 'predefinedCredentialType'/'postmarkApi' config below was never backed by a real credential in this n8n instance and had no effect. Also built its body via bodyParameters (form-encoded) instead of a real JSON body, and never included a From address, which Postmark requires. Same fix as Agent 3's Postmark node -- see its note for the full explanation.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ From: $vars.POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL, To: $('GET Lead').first().json.lead.email, Subject: $json.subject, TextBody: $json.body, MessageStream: 'outbound' }) }}

nodes.name: Check Postmark Result
nodes.notes: Postmark can return HTTP 200 with a non-zero ErrorCode in its response body (e.g. an inactive recipient) -- checking HTTP status alone isn't enough to know the send actually succeeded.

nodes.name: POST /webhooks/inbound
nodes.notes: In production, prefer a Cal.com/Google Calendar 'booking confirmed' webhook to fire this instead of firing immediately after the invite email — this models the simpler 'propose a link' flow from the spec.
